sections.title: 49.1 Change Data Capture — CDC
sections.body:
Enterprise knowledge sources continuously change.

Instead of re-indexing everything every night, use incremental synchronization where the source supports it.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Source database or document repository] --> B[Change events]
    B --> C[Event queue]
    C --> D{Event type}
    D -->|Create| E[New ingestion]
    D -->|Update| F[Versioned re-indexing]
    D -->|Delete| G[Remove active evidence]
    D -->|Permission change| H[Update ACLs and caches]
    E --> I[Consistency validation]
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
```

Teach event ordering, sequence numbers, duplicate events, late-arriving updates, tombstones, reconciliation jobs and synchronization lag.

diagram.title: Visual flow — 49.1 Change Data Capture — CDC

steps.label: Load
steps.narration: Loading converts PDFs, DOCX, CSV, HTML and other sources into a consistent document object with text plus metadata.

steps.label: Clean
steps.narration: Cleaning removes boilerplate, normalizes unicode, strips headers/footers, and prepares text so chunking and embeddings stay high quality.

steps.label: Chunk
steps.narration: Chunking splits documents into retrieval units. Size and overlap control whether evidence is complete enough without adding noise.

steps.label: Embed
steps.narration: Embedding turns each chunk into a dense vector so semantically similar questions and passages can be matched.

steps.label: Index
steps.narration: Indexing stores vectors (and often sparse signals) for fast nearest-neighbor search with filters for tenant, source, or time. Instead of re-indexing everything every night, use incremental synchronization where the source supports it.

steps.label: Retrieve
steps.narration: Retrieval finds the Top-K chunks for a query using dense, sparse, or hybrid search before generation.

steps.label: Generate
steps.narration: Generation builds an answer from the retrieved context. Good prompts require evidence, citations, and abstention when support is weak.

sections.title: 49.2 Deletion propagation
sections.body:
A deleted document may still exist in multiple locations.

**Delete document request**

Deletion workflows need to distinguish immediate access revocation from physical removal according to retention rules and backup policies.

A reconciliation job should detect records that remain searchable after deletion.
